comment: K1 atlas cell map, Kenney edition: every cell is either ONE PNG file under src/iso/kenny OR an ordered multi-storey 'stack' of layer PNGs. Each single cell carries: name, png (repo path relative to src/iso/kenny), kind, footprint. A stacked 'standing' building replaces png with 'stack': a bottom-to-top array of layer descriptors ({ png }) — base first, middle floors, roof on top (2-6 layers). The packer resolves each distinct (png, tint) layer once into a shared packed sprite and emits a composite manifest entry whose 'parts' tell the renderer how to draw the stack bottom-to-top; depth-sort and picking treat the whole stack as ONE object on its footprint. Single-png cells (terrain, roads, the one-piece industries) are unchanged and additive with stacks. kind: 'ground' = a flat Kenney block (132x64 diamond over a base skirt of whatever depth the source PNG has) — the packer anchors it by its measured GROUND ROW (the base diamond's left/right corner row) and REJECTS it unless that row sits at y~32 with ~full width (the spec's flat-only filter: slope/ramp tiles fail). K-FIX-1: sprites are never cropped or height-normalised; Kenney tiles are designed to be different heights and are anchored at their shared ground line; 'standing' = a building, anchored by the ground row of its base diamond so it stands flush on the tile; 'vehicle' = anchored bottom-centre on the tile surface. Anchors are always COMPUTED by the packer from the pixels — there is no hand-authored anchor, box, crop, compose, sprite-id or generator field anywhere in this file. Derived art (rail set, crossing, placement glows) is pre-drawn by tools/make-derived-art.mjs into src/iso/kenny/derived and referenced like any Kenney PNG.
